description: 4-person full-stack team turning NASA data into tools people can act on. We're building TerraAlerta NISAR for Dancing with the SARs: early warning of ground deformation and landslide risk with new NISAR L-band SAR + FIRMS + DEM. Explainable risk map for civil defense. Skills: React, Python/ML, GIS, APIs, 3D, UI/UX, pitch. Want: SAR/InSAR, GDAL/raster, QA/video.
summary: TerraAlerta NISAR helps Civil Defense teams decide which forested slopes to inspect first after heavy rain. For Dancing with the SARs, we built an interactive dashboard that displays results from repeat NASA-ISRO radar observations in Sao Sebastiao, Brazil, alongside a map of estimated inspection priorities under simulated rainfall. Brumadinho is a second study area for terrain triage near mining operations.
details:
Inspection workflow. A user selects a study area, explores the color-coded grid and filters sectors by estimated priority. The user can set a hypothetical 72-hour rainfall total and recalculate a sector assessment and technical bulletin to plan field visits.

Demonstration result. The Sao Sebastiao baseline uses a geotechnical slope stability model and a scenario of 150 mm of rain in 72 hours. The map ranks 28 cells as high priority, covering about 2.4 km2 in that scenario. The interface identifies measured radar returns, slope derived from public elevation data and estimated priority scores.

Surface observations and validation. We used a 12-day NISAR radar pair to display coherence and displacement along the radar's line of sight in Sao Sebastiao. Typical displacement magnitudes are close to the team's estimated noise level, so we treat this pair as exploratory. The landslide catalog check found sparse local records. Our next step is to compare inspection priorities against mapped landslide scars and field records.

Implementation. Python and FastAPI serve the geospatial data and scenario calculations. React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL and react-globe.gl provide the web interface and maps.
